issues.description: The template's Main.java contains commented example instantiations of Seal, Pig, and Goat using two constructor parameters (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")). The problem statement and UML specify that animals have only a name attribute and that constructors should initialize class attributes (single name). The provided solution implements single-parameter constructors (e.g., Seal(String name)). This mismatch in constructor parameters in the template may confuse students about the intended constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's example instantiations consistent with the specification and solution by changing the commented examples in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to use single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")). Alternatively, if two-argument constructors were intended, update the problem statement/UML and the solution to include and document the additional attribute.

issues.description: Constructor usage for animal classes is inconsistent across artifacts: the template Main.java calls Seal, Pig, and Goat constructors with two arguments (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), implying a second attribute, while the problem statement/UML and the solution use single-argument constructors that initialize only the animal's name (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle")). This mismatch creates confusion about the required class attributes and constructor signatures (students may implement constructors that do not match the provided Main usage or the UML/spec).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the animal constructor usage consistent across all artifacts. Either update the template Main.java to use single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky")) to match the UML/problem statement and solution, or revise the UML/problem statement and solution to include and document the second attribute (and corresponding constructor parameter) for all Animal subclasses.
